sourcedFrom: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. (2014)
cleanIntro: Thompson/Center's own cleaning procedure for the G2 Contender, from the one book T/C prints for both the pistol and the rifle. The G2 Contender is a single-shot break-action: pulling up and back on the trigger guard spur unlocks the barrel and it tips down at the muzzle. Its hammer carries a three-position firing pin selector (centerfire, center safe, rimfire). The routine strip is the forend off and the barrel off the frame by its hinge pin, and the book says that is as far as the gun comes apart.

steps.title: Hammer at rest, selector centred, pull the trigger guard spur
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction and finger away from the trigger, with the hammer in the At Rest position and the firing pin selector in its center position, pull up and back on the trigger guard spur. The barrel unlocks and falls open, exposing the chamber.
steps.prose: On the G2 Contender the trigger guard is the action release. The selector on the hammer has three positions, and the center one is the one T/C marks SAFE: put it there before you open the gun. T/C's tip is to put your finger low on the spur for leverage and give it a quick pull.
steps.quote: With your finger away from the trigger, with the hammer in the “AT REST” position and the firing pin selector in the center position (FIGURE 10a), open the action by pulling up and back on the trigger guard spur (FIGURES 11a & 11b).
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. — INSPECTING, p.13
steps.warn: ANY TIME THAT YOU HANDLE A G2 CONTENDER®, OPEN THE ACTION AND ENSURE THAT IT IS UNLOADED.

steps.title: Take the cartridge out of the chamber
steps.action: With the hammer in its safe, at-rest position, tip the barrel open and take any cartridge out of the chamber by hand.
steps.prose: The G2 Contender is a single shot, so the chamber is the only place a round can be. Take it out and set it away from the bench before you go on. If the gun was just fired and a round failed to go off, T/C says to keep the muzzle in a safe direction and wait 10 seconds before opening the barrel.
steps.quote: With the hammer in the “SAFE” position, (FIGURE 30) tip the barrel open and remove the ammunition from the chamber (FIGURE 31 & 32).
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. — UNLOADING, p.21

steps.title: Look into the chamber and through the bore
steps.action: Look into the barrel from the breech end and confirm there is no cartridge in the chamber, then confirm the bore is clear and free of obstructions.
steps.prose: With the barrel tipped down you can see straight down the bore from the breech. T/C asks for this check every time the gun leaves your hand, is cleaned, handed over, transported or stored.
steps.quote: Look into the barrel from the breech end to make sure there is no cartridge in the chamber (FIGURE 12).
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. — INSPECTING, p.13

steps.title: Confirm the chamber empty, then close the barrel
steps.action: With the hammer at rest and the muzzle in a safe direction, open the action once more, make sure the chamber is unloaded, then close the barrel.
steps.prose: T/C's takedown starts with the gun closed: the forend screws come out with the barrel shut on the frame. The book splits the gun into three groups: the frame assembly with the fire control inside it, the barrel, and the grip or stock with the forend.
steps.quote: With the hammer in the “At Rest” position, point the firearm in a safe direction, open the action and make sure that the chamber is unloaded. Close the barrel.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. — TAKEDOWN OF THE G2 CONTENDER, p.25

steps.title: Forend screws out, forend off
steps.action: Turn the forend screw or screws out counterclockwise, as viewed from the bottom of the gun, and take the forend off the barrel.
steps.prose: Depending on the barrel there may be one forend screw or more. Keep them together: the same screws go back in to hold the forend on. Rifle, shotgun, pistol and muzzleloading barrels may each need their own forend.
steps.quote: Remove the forend screw(s). Turn these screws out counterclockwise (as viewed from the bottom of the gun). Remove the forend from the barrel.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. — TAKEDOWN OF THE G2 CONTENDER, p.26

steps.title: Open the barrel, tap out the hinge pin, barrel off
steps.action: Open the barrel again to take the tension off the hinge pin, tap the hinge pin out in either direction, and take the barrel off the frame.
steps.prose: The hinge pin is what anchors the barrel lug to the frame, and with the barrel open it is no longer under load. It comes out either way. With the barrel off, you have the frame assembly, the barrel, and the grip or stock with the forend.
steps.quote: Open the barrel again to remove any tension on the hinge pin and remove the barrel hinge pin by tapping it out (in either direction). Remove the barrel from the frame.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. — TAKEDOWN OF THE G2 CONTENDER, p.26

steps.title: Stop here: this is the extent of disassembly
steps.action: Go no further. Barrel off the frame is as far as T/C has the G2 Contender taken apart. Any other service goes to Thompson/Center Customer Service.
steps.prose: The hammer, sear and firing pin are housed inside the frame and the hinge pin, and the book publishes no procedure for them. The grip and grip cap stay on the frame.
steps.quote: This diagram shows the extent to which the G2 Contender® should be disassembled (FIGURE 34). If other service is required, contact the Thompson/Center Customer Service Department.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. — DISASSEMBLY, p.26
steps.warn: Never disassemble your firearm beyond the procedures outlined in this manual. Improper disassembly or re-assembly of your firearm may be dangerous and can lead to serious injury or death.

steps.title: Brass brush and solvent through the bore and chamber
steps.action: Scrub the firing residue out of the bore and the chamber with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent.
steps.prose: A properly fitted brush is one made for your bore, and G2 Contender barrels come in many calibers, so match the brush to the barrel in front of you. T/C's basic kit is a brass bore brush and a jag of the right size, solvent, oil, cotton patches, and a rod long enough to push them all the way through the barrel.
steps.quote: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and chamber using a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.23
steps.warn: Ammoniated solvents or other strong alkaline solvents, should not be used on any Thompson/Center firearm.

steps.title: Dry patch to finish the bore
steps.action: Finish by running a dry cotton patch through the bore to lift out the loosened residue and the solvent.
steps.prose: The dry patch is the last thing through the bore in T/C's procedure. Solvent left in the bore is not lubrication.
steps.quote: Finish the bore cleaning process by running a dry cotton cloth patch through the bore to remove residue and solvent.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.23

steps.title: Wipe the outside, then a light coat of oil on the metal
steps.action: Clean the outside of the gun with a non-abrasive cloth, then put a light coat of good firearm oil on the metal parts, inside and out.
steps.prose: Inside and out includes the frame and the barrel lug where the hinge pin runs, which are easy to reach with the barrel off. In a cold climate, T/C says to use an oil weight that will not congeal and slow the parts down.
steps.quote: After cleaning, lightly coat the metal parts, internal and external with a high quality firearm oil.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.23

steps.title: Take the fingerprints off
steps.action: Wipe any cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints off the outside surfaces of the gun.
steps.prose: T/C's reason is corrosion: moisture from your fingers left on the steel can start rust.
steps.quote: Remove any gun cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints from the outside surfaces of the firearm. (Finger moisture, if left, could start a corrosion process.)
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.24

steps.title: .410 choke barrels: brush out the lead after shot loads
steps.action: On a 45 Colt/.410 barrel with an internal choke, after heavy use of shot cartridges, clean the barrel and the choke tube with a tight-fitting stiff bore brush to take out the lead build-up.
steps.prose: Barrels without an internal choke skip this screen. Take the tube out with the choke wrench first: counterclockwise removes it.
steps.quote: After heavy use of shot cartridges, clean the barrel and choke tube with a tight fitting stiff bore brush to remove any accumulation of lead.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. — INSTALLATION OF CHOKE TUBE, p.29

steps.title: Keep the choke tube threads clean and lightly lubed
steps.action: Clean the threads on the choke tube and in the barrel and keep them lightly lubricated with a good anti-seize lubricant.
steps.prose: Clogged threads are why a tube will not screw in easily, and a tube forced in can cross-thread. Only T/C choke tubes go in a G2 Contender.
steps.quote: The threads of your T/C choke tubes should be kept clean and lightly lubed at all times
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. — INSTALLATION of CHOKE TUBES in G2 CONTENDER 410 GAUGE BARREL, p.28
steps.warn: NEVER ATTEMPT TO USE ANY OTHER BRAND CHOKE TUBE IN A THOMPSON/CENTER G2 CONTENDER®.

steps.title: Check for wear every time you clean
steps.action: Look the gun over for signs of wear each time you clean it. If you find wear, do not use the gun: return it to Thompson/Center for service or have a qualified gunsmith check it.
steps.prose: The same book says any maintenance, adjustment or service it does not specify must be done by a qualified gunsmith using genuine Thompson/Center parts.
steps.quote: Every time you clean your firearm, check it for signs of wear. If wear is noted, do not use the firearm. Return it to Thompson/Center for service or have it checked by a qualified gunsmith.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual G2 Contender® Pistol & Rifle — Copyright © 2014 Smith & Wesson Corp. — MAINTENANCE BEFORE STORAGE, p.25

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the G2 Contender, and this guide does not invent one. Thompson/Center's book ends the disassembly at the takedown (forend off, hinge pin out, barrel off the frame) and states on page 26 that this is the extent to which the G2 Contender should be disassembled, with other service going to Thompson/Center Customer Service. On page 23 it says never to disassemble the firearm beyond its field stripping and inspection sections. The hammer, sear and firing pin are housed within the frame and the hinge pin and are not for the bench.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Properly fitted brass brush dipped in firearm solvent through the bore and chamber
Dry cotton patch through the bore to finish
Do not use ammoniated or strong alkaline solvents on a Thompson/Center firearm

cleaning.name: METAL & EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe the outside with a non-abrasive cloth
Light coat of firearm oil on the metal parts, inside and out
Wipe off cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints
For long storage, oil the bore, chamber and internal surfaces

cleaning.name: CHOKE TUBE (.410 BARRELS)
tasks: Choke tube out with the wrench, counterclockwise
After heavy shot use, stiff bore brush through the barrel and the tube to remove lead
Clean the tube and barrel threads; keep them lightly lubed with anti-seize
⛔ The choke tube must come out before ball ammunition, rifled slugs or buckshot are fired

reassembly: Before assembly, put a light film of quality gun oil on all the metal parts.
The forend must be off the barrel before the barrel goes on the frame. Insert the barrel lug into the frame.
Line up the hinge pin holes in the barrel and the frame and insert the hinge pin. Centre it so it does not stick out of either side, then tip the barrel up and closed on the frame.
Place the rear of the forend against the receiver, line up the holes in the forend over the holes in the barrel, and secure it with the supplied forend screws.

.410 choke barrels: refit the choke tube clockwise with the muzzle pointed away from you. It should screw in easily by hand; if it does not, the threads may be clogged or crossed, so never force it. Snug it with the wrench and do not over-tighten it.
fncheck: With the gun unloaded, check that the hammer and trigger work properly before you load and fire it. T/C requires this check after reassembly but prints no step-by-step test for it. Open and close the action with the trigger guard spur and confirm the barrel locks up closed, and leave the firing pin selector in its center safe position when you are done. If you dry-fire to check the hammer, T/C recommends it only with snap caps of the right cartridge designation. If the gun feels or sounds different from normal, do not fire it: contact Thompson/Center Customer Support.
breakOpen: pull up and back on the trigger guard spur and let the barrel tip down.
